rendered: The premise does not match the paper. It does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich cathodes. Its stated conclusion is the opposite, in its words: Overall, this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]. The lithium leaching it measured is also small. The paper says the leached fraction rises with nickel content, but even Ni-rich NMC 811 shows only minimal[2] leaching, at about ~3 wt%[3] after a week. XRD, Raman and XPS showed no bulk structural change and only minor surface changes. The paper does note a trade-off: aqueous-processed cells retain slightly less capacity than NMP-processed cells, but it judges them still to show: the aqueous-processed NMC 811 cells still demonstrate very good cycling[4] performance. Its remaining caveats concern formulation, which must be handled properly to avoid issues such as: There are several other issues that can arise with NMC 811 aqueous processing if formulation chemistry is not handled properly[5].
